newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia official calls for compromise in Serbia.
newsitem.headline: Russia official calls for compromise in Serbia.

text.p: A senior Russian official on Monday said Moscow was worried over mounting tension in Serbia and urged its government and political opposition to look for a compromise.

Deputy Foreign Minister Igor Ivanov, who visited Belgrade late last month, told ORT television that bloody clashes between protesters and riot police which had started on Sunday night in Serbian capital Belgrade could not solve any problems.

"The aim of my trip was to make the leadership of this country and the opposition know that Moscow was worried by the situation and urge them to start dialogue and promptly find way out of the crisis," Ivanov said.
More than 100 anti-government protesters were injured in the bloodiest political violence seen for years in Serbian capital Belgrade on Sunday night.
The United States and its European allies condemned police actions but stopped short of calling for any international sanctions against Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.
Moscow, Milosevic's long-time ally, has not officially taken sides in the dispute between the embattled president and the opposition over results of recent local elections which he had annuled.
"The main thing now is to stay away from violence," Ivanov said. "What appened last night, namely the clashes which led to even greated tension, are not the way out."
